name: add_tests_aspnet_webapplicationfactory
description: Asks the model to write xUnit tests for an already-correct ASP.NET Core minimal API using WebApplicationFactory
prompts: The ASP.NET Core minimal API project at the repo root (app.csproj, net8.0; Program.cs already working, do not modify it) exposes two endpoints: GET /ping, which returns HTTP 200 with JSON {"message": "pong"}; and GET /square/{n}, which returns HTTP 200 with JSON {"input": n, "result": n*n} for an integer route parameter n. There is already a test project at tests/tests.csproj (referencing the app project and the xunit/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing packages; do not modify tests.csproj) but no test file yet. Add a new file at tests/EndpointTests.cs containing xUnit tests that use Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing's WebApplicationFactory<Program> to exercise both endpoints in-process: one [Fact] test that calls GET /ping and asserts the response is successful and the message is "pong", and another [Fact] test that calls GET /square/5 and asserts the response is successful and the JSON result equals 25. Do not modify Program.cs or tests.csproj.

setup_files.app.csproj:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- tests/ has its own project; without this the SDK's default glob
         compiles tests/*.cs into the app itself, where xunit isn't referenced -->
    <Compile Remove="tests/**" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
setup_files.tests/tests.csproj:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.11.1" />
    <PackageReference Include="xunit" Version="2.9.2" />
    <PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.2" />
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing" Version="8.0.10" />
    <PackageReference Include="coverlet.collector" Version="6.0.2" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="../app.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path('Program.cs')
TEST_CMD = 'dotnet test tests/tests.csproj'
# Each entry is one mutant: a list of (original, replacement) edits applied
# together. Every `original` anchor must appear exactly once in the pristine
# implementation - which also enforces the prompt's "do not modify it".
MUTANTS = [ [ [ "new { message = \"pong\" }", "new { message = \"pong!\" }" ] ], [ [ "result = n * n", "result = n + n" ] ] ]

def run_tests():
    # Python caches bytecode by (mtime-seconds, size); a same-length
    # mutant written within the same second would run the STALE pyc of
    # the unmutated source. Clear the cache so every run compiles fresh.
    shutil.rmtree('__pycache__', ignore_errors=True)
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode

src = IMPL.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
for group in MUTANTS:
    for old, _new in group:
        assert src.count(old) == 1, (
            f'protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to change it '
            f'(anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})')

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f'model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})'

try:
    for i, group in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        mutated = src
        for old, new in group:
            mutated = mutated.replace(old, new)
        IMPL.write_text(mutated, encoding='utf-8')
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f'mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately broken '
            f'implementation, so they do not actually verify the required behavior')
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding='utf-8')

print('PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {n} mutants)'.format(n=len(MUTANTS)))
